free_tier.stated: No free tier read. The live pricing page lists '7 Days Charged at $3.94 USD for 7 day block', '1 Month Charged at $9.95 USD per month' and '12 Months Charged at $83.58 USD per 12 months', each with a '30-Day Money-Back Guarantee'.
free_tier.notes: The cheapest yearly price is $83.58 for 12 months ($6.97 per month, 'Save 59%'). The 7-day block is the cheapest entry price. No trial page was read.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an exit address, not an object
per_object_cap.notes: No object is stored; the constraint is the 6-device cap in limits.

retention.stated: not applicable: a live tunnel and a rented exit address, not stored bytes
retention.notes: The vendor says its VPN servers have no hard drives and that it keeps no user logs; no byte retention applies.

egress.terms: The pricing page states a price per term and no byte allowance, cap or per-GB price; the FAQ has a question 'Does Oeck ever limit customer usage?' whose answer was not on the pages read. metered is false on the absence of any stated byte figure, and no byte was counted through a tunnel.
egress.free_allowance: none published: the pages price a term, not a volume

interface_detail: Vendor apps (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux) and OpenVPN configuration files that list every server, per the FAQ. No SOCKS5 endpoint, API or WireGuard configuration is named on the first-party pages read. No interface term names a VPN tunnel.
tooling: The vendor's apps or any OpenVPN client with the vendor's .ovpn files; port forwarding is configured on a device profile in the account area.
chaining: A compute node runs an OpenVPN client with a vendor .ovpn file, so its traffic leaves at the region's exit address (a random server in the region for OpenVPN); a Worker cannot dial the tunnel directly and no proxy endpoint is documented.

limits.value: 6 devices at once: 'You may have up to 6 devices logged in to our network concurrently'
an OpenVPN client gets a random server in the chosen region, the apps get the server the network picks by load

limits_note: Three facts no limit kind names. (1) The first-party pages read name no protocol list other than OpenVPN config files; WireGuard, UDP, a SOCKS5 endpoint and an obfuscation mode are unverified: not stated on any first-party page read. (2) Registration: whether sign-up is open today is unverified: the register page was not read; the pricing page carries Buy buttons. (3) Residential claim: the vendor's home page says a 'residential IP smartRouting' is built into the network, while its FAQ says the streaming exits are on a proxy network of colocated, dedicated and virtual private servers; it is a vendor claim that no page lets anyone check.
binding_note: No byte quota is stated, so the first stated limit is the 6-concurrent-device cap; the torrent-region rule decides where BitTorrent may run. No rate was measured.

identity_cost.detail: An email address is required to create an account ('we need to be able to get in touch with you'). Payments run through Stripe, Coinbase and 2Checkout, so a card or cryptocurrency is how the plan is paid; the sign-up form itself was not read, so the exact field list is unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: unverified: whether the service itself is up, since only marketing and FAQ pages were read and no tunnel was brought up. Per the FAQ the company is incorporated in Hong Kong with a planned move to Singapore.
confidence_note: Documented from the vendor's pricing, features and FAQ pages. Registration status and the protocol list are unverified. Measured would need an account, a tunnel per protocol and the register and downloads pages.

evidence.proved: The 12 Months plan is charged $83.58 USD per 12 months.
The 12 Months plan is shown as $6.97 per month, 'Save 59%'; the 1 Month plan is $9.95 per month and the 7 Days block $3.94.

evidence.quote: We issue you ports and you enable ports you select on your device profile(s).
evidence.proved: Advanced Port Forwarding: the vendor issues ports, the user enables them on a device profile and names the target port, and each port gets a custom domain name.

evidence.quote: You may have up to 6 devices logged in to our network concurrently
evidence.proved: Up to 6 devices may be connected at once.

evidence.quote: In order to make the user experience the best we possibly can, we need to be able to get in touch with you.
evidence.proved: An email address is required to create an account; the FAQ lists password resets, ticket replies and expiry notices as its purposes.

evidence.quote: Oeck uses Stripe, Coinbase and 2Checkout to process all of our payments.
evidence.proved: Payments are processed by Stripe, Coinbase and 2Checkout.

evidence.quote: If you want to see our full server list, it is available in the OpenVPN config files.
evidence.proved: OpenVPN configuration files carry the full server list; a user can connect with an OpenVPN client instead of the apps.
The features page lists AES-256 encryption and a 4096-bit key exchange.

evidence.quote: The second is the Proxy Network (opNetwork).
evidence.proved: Streaming exits are on a separate proxy network (opNetwork) of colocated, dedicated and virtual private servers, reached by a multi-hop from the VPN network.

evidence.quote: Our revolutionary residential IP smartRouting is built in to the OECK network.
evidence.proved: The vendor's home page says a residential IP smartRouting is built into the network: a vendor claim for streaming unblock, with no ASN or sample address published.

price_per_tb_month: USD 6.97 per month on the 12 Months plan (USD 83.58 per 12 months); a subscription price, not a per-TB price
notes: Port forwarding: Yes: 'Advanced Port Forwarding', ports issued by the vendor and enabled per device profile, with a custom domain name per port that works from any region.
